correctness.adjudication: COUNTEREVIDENCE: once raw SQLite is given the same admission contract, this gate-level semantic-safety accuracy is not unique to Clay. Preserve Clay as semantic authority/typed contract and compile its rules into the simplest efficient runtime mechanism.

latency_interpretation: Do not promote the latency ratio as an engine superiority result. The SQL arm crosses the Python sqlite3 API per single-case query and the batch materializes result tuples. This benchmark exists primarily to falsify the unique-accuracy claim under matched semantics.
shared_preprocessing_boundary: Canonical row serialization and SHA-256 construction are excluded from both timed gate arms; stock SQLite has no built-in SHA-256. Both arms receive already-computed receipt fields.

keep: Clay/ClayCode as semantic authority for epoch, provenance, ambiguity, verification, replay and effect-boundary contracts
SQLite/B-tree/SQL predicates as valid compiled execution mechanisms when they implement those semantics exactly
differential tests proving compiled mechanism equivalence
reject: claim that the storage engine itself creates semantic safety
claim that Clay must physically replace conventional database mechanisms to be more useful for Frank/Clay
using a deliberately weak row-store baseline as sufficient proof of Clay-specific accuracy

next_falsifiers: self-hosted Ubuntu replication of this matched contract benchmark
same-contract concurrent writer and snapshot isolation tests
whole model-input Assembly comparison including provenance receipt construction, not gate-only microbenchmarks
real repo-native held-out retrieval episodes with independently adjudicated answer/tool-choice outcomes
